Definition: from G2596 and ναρκάω (to be numb); to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive):--be burdensome (chargeable).
BiblicalUsage: Paul was determined not to be burdensome to the Corinthians, and he asks what they were made inferior in, except that he himself was not burdensome to them. He says the third time he is ready to come and will not be burdensome, for he seeks not theirs but them. The word is Paul's pride in reverse: he boasts that he cost them nothing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a minister who refuses to be a burden is showing the gospel, not just preaching it. I hold that the church is not a purse to be emptied, and the best gift a teacher can give is himself.
